summary:
MASKAYBOX is an interactive web application that transforms the exploration of our planet into a multisensory experience through data sonification and scientific visualizations from NASA. Using a three-dimensional globe, users can explore different regions of the world and discover Earth-related phenomena through datasets covering nighttime lights, ocean temperatures, vegetation, atmospheric electrical activity, air quality, and atmospheric rivers.

By analyzing visual features such as brightness, spatial distribution, elevation, and temperature, the system establishes mappings between data attributes and musical parameters to generate auditory representations and original soundscapes.

The experience integrates 360° orbital exploration, audio playback and processing, a bilingual virtual guide, and alternative interaction mechanisms. With an accessibility-centered approach, MASKAYBOX aims to expand the possibilities of scientific exploration and interpretation, particularly for people with partial or total visual impairments, using sound as a complementary tool to understand and experience the phenomena that shape our planet.
details:
MASKAYBOX

MASKAYBOX is an interactive web application that transforms the exploration of geospatial information into a multisensory experience by combining three-dimensional visualization, data sonification, and accessibility tools. Developed using modular JavaScript, HTML5, and CSS3, it leverages Three.js (r128) and custom GLSL shaders to create a three-dimensional environment centered around a digital globe, allowing users to navigate different regions and explore scientific representations of our planet.

The application incorporates several themes related to Earth's natural phenomena, drawing on resources from NASA's Earth Information Center (EIC) and other NASA scientific sources. These include nighttime lights, represented through VIIRS Black Marble data; ocean temperatures and currents, using resources related to GHRSST MUR; forest height and distribution, based on GEDI data; lightning events detected from space through LIS; and different representations of air quality and atmospheric rivers.

The core of MASKAYBOX is its sonification system, which transforms characteristics of scientific visualizations into auditory representations. By analyzing properties such as brightness, spatial distribution, elevation, and temperature, the system establishes mappings to musical parameters such as pitch, rhythm, volume, and intensity. These relationships enable the development of sound representations tailored to each scientific theme, while aiming to preserve an understandable connection between the characteristics of the original data and their auditory interpretation.

Audio processing combines real-time synthesis and playback mechanisms through the Web Audio API with original soundscapes produced and edited in REAPER. Integrating different audio resources and sound characteristics makes it possible to create auditory experiences that accompany geographical exploration and provide a complementary perspective on Earth's phenomena.

One of the project's fundamental aspects is its commitment to scientific accessibility. MASKAYBOX incorporates a bilingual virtual guide (Spanish and English), developed using the Web Speech API, which interprets voice commands through approximate matching mechanisms and provides guidance throughout the exploration process. Additionally, it integrates audio descriptions and haptic feedback through the Vibration API on compatible devices, aiming to facilitate navigation and access to information for blind and low-vision users.

The originality of MASKAYBOX lies in its integration of three-dimensional visualization technologies, image analysis, algorithmic sonification, sound production, and voice assistance within a single interactive experience. Rather than limiting scientific information to images and graphical representations, the project proposes sound as an additional medium for exploration and interpretation, expanding the possibilities for accessing knowledge about our planet.
